intro: Kuala Lumpur is a young, fast-changing capital where Malay, Chinese and Indian neighbourhoods sit side by side under some of the tallest towers on earth: colonial arcades around Merdeka Square, incense-filled Chinatown lanes, a wooden Malay village in the shadow of the Petronas Towers, and rainforest on a hill in the city centre. This three-night leg moves from old KL (day 1) to caves, kampung and towers (day 2), then the planned capital Putrajaya and New Year's Eve fireworks (day 3). The new View at 118 deck (scheduled to open 15 Dec 2026, on the world's second-tallest building) and a rooftop-pool hotel for New Year's Eve are the two things to book now.

stay.area: KLCC / Golden Triangle (Jalan Ampang, Jalan Kia Peng, Jalan Sultan Ismail)
stay.why: Best base for New Year's Eve: you can walk to KLCC Park for the Petronas Towers fireworks and walk back while roads are closed and Grab is surging. Most of the rooftop infinity pools with tower views are here. Pools generally close at 22:00-23:00, so plan a sunset/evening swim and watch the midnight fireworks from a tower-facing room or the hotel's New Year party; ask for a high floor facing the Petronas Towers in writing.
example_hotels: Imperial Lexis Kuala Lumpur - 51st-floor Sky Infinity Pool (about 07:00-22:00) and glass-floored SkyDeck looking at Petronas Towers, KL Tower and Merdeka 118; guests only
The FACE Suites - 51st-floor infinity pool with Petronas Towers + KL Tower view (about 07:00-22:00); suites with kitchens
Banyan Tree Kuala Lumpur - 57th-floor pool, close-up Petronas view; Vertigo rooftop bar
W Kuala Lumpur - 12th-floor WET Deck pool facing the towers; ticketed New Year's Eve party on the deck
Traders Hotel Kuala Lumpur - next to KLCC Park; SkyBar sits around the rooftop pool facing the towers (NYE is ticketed); pool closes ~18:00
Somerset Kuala Lumpur (serviced apartments) - pool with tower view open until ~23:00, cheaper option

stay.why: Street-food and nightlife hub (Jalan Alor, Changkat), with monorail and MRT; 15-20 min walk to KLCC. The New Year street party here and at The Exchange TRX (midnight fireworks, rooftop City Park) is easier to move around than KLCC Park.
example_hotels: Mercure Kuala Lumpur Shaw Parade (20th-floor pool, budget)
The RuMa Hotel and Residences (Jalan Kia Peng, between the two areas)

stay.why: Walkable to Merdeka Square, Chinatown and the View at 118; quieter at night. Park Hyatt sits inside Merdeka 118 itself (lobby on level 75, 30 m infinity pool, ~US$400/night) and hosts a countdown at Cacao on level 75 - a high, calm view across to the KLCC fireworks about 2 km away.
example_hotels: The Majestic Hotel Kuala Lumpur (1932 colonial hotel by the old railway station)

arrival: From KLIA (T1 or T2) take the KLIA Ekspres non-stop to KL Sentral: 28 min from T1, 33 min from T2, every 15-20 min from about 05:00 to past midnight. Single fare RM55 (~US$13) until 31 Dec 2026, rising to RM65 (~US$15.50) from 1 Jan 2027; tap a contactless bank card at the gate or buy at kliaekspres.com. From KL Sentral a Grab to KLCC/Bukit Bintang hotels takes 10-20 min (RM10-20, ~US$2.50-5). A direct Grab from KLIA to the city is 50-70 min and about RM75-110 (~US$18-26). Before you fly, fill in the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online within 3 days of arrival; most Western passports then use the automatic e-gates.
getting_around: Rapid KL trains (LRT, MRT, monorail) cover almost every stop; fares RM1-6 (~US$0.25-1.50). Tap a contactless Visa/Mastercard at the gates, or buy a Touch 'n Go card (RM10 + top-up) at stations or 7-Eleven, which also works on KTM Komuter and buses. Use the Grab app for everything else: inner-city rides are usually RM8-20 (~US$2-5) and Putrajaya/airport trips RM50-110. Street taxis often refuse the meter. The free GoKL city buses loop through Bukit Bintang, KLCC and Chinatown. KL is hot and has few pedestrian crossings; the covered, air-conditioned walkway from Pavilion to KLCC (about 1.2 km) is the best way between those two areas. Google Maps transit directions are reliable; MyRapid PULSE shows live train times and holiday changes.
weather: Late December is warm and humid: about 24-33 C, with a high chance of short, heavy thunderstorms in the afternoon or evening (December is one of KL's wetter months; January is a bit drier). Mornings are usually clear, so do outdoor and hill sights early and keep museums, malls or the hotel pool for 14:00-17:00. Carry a small umbrella. Sunrise is about 07:10-07:15 and sunset about 19:10-19:15 (29-31 Dec); good light lasts until ~19:40.
etiquette: Mosques (Putra, Iron Mosque, Masjid Negara): non-Muslims visit only outside prayer times; cover arms and legs, women cover hair - robes and headscarves are lent free at the entrance; shoes off; don't enter prayer halls. Hindu temples (Batu Caves, Sri Mahamariamman, Brickfields): shoes off at the door, shoulders and knees covered (Batu Caves lends/rents sarongs at the foot of the stairs). Chinese temples are relaxed but don't point feet at altars or photograph worshippers close up. Use your right hand to give and receive. Cards are accepted almost everywhere except hawker stalls, small temples and the KL Forest Eco Park (cash only) - carry RM100-200 in small notes. Restaurants add 10% service + 8% service tax (SST); tipping isn't expected. Scams to avoid: unmetered taxis at stations and malls (use Grab), 'gem' or card-game invitations, overpriced 'guides' at Batu Caves, and fake designer goods on Petaling Street. Grab bag-snatching by motorbike happens: walk on the inside of the pavement with bags away from the road. Long-tailed macaques at Batu Caves and Bukit Nanas grab food and plastic bags.

days.title: Arrival & old KL: gardens, Merdeka Square, Chinatown, sunset from Merdeka 118
days.summary: A walking day through the colonial and Chinese heart of KL, with the rainforest-like Perdana Gardens as a gentle first stop after the flight. Afternoon is Merdeka Square, Central Market and Chinatown's lanes and temples, all within 15 minutes' walk of each other, finishing 500 m up on Merdeka 118 for sunset and the calm TRX rooftop park as the towers light up.
notes: Assumes landing by about 08:00. If you land later, cut in this order: Islamic Arts Museum, Old Railway Station, Perdana Gardens - keep Merdeka Square, Chinatown and Merdeka 118.

Timing: Merdeka 118 is set for 17:45-19:45 so you are on the 115th floor for sunset (~19:12) and blue hour; book a timed View at 118 ticket online now - it is scheduled to open on 15 Dec 2026 (two weeks before you arrive) and slots around sunset will sell out over the holidays.
The middle of the day (12:00-16:00) is hot; the Islamic Arts Museum, Central Market and the Textile Museum on Merdeka Square are air-conditioned shelters if a storm hits.
Tuesday: almost everything is open. Many small shops in Kampung Attap / Zhongshan Building close Mon-Tue, so skip that add-on today.
15-night version (arriving Wed 30 Dec): see KL2 notes for the merged day.

stops.name: Arrive: KLIA Ekspres to KL Sentral, drop bags
stops.description: Clear immigration (MDAC done online beforehand), then follow signs to the KLIA Ekspres; trains leave every 15-20 minutes and reach KL Sentral in under 35 minutes. KL Sentral is the city's main rail hub, linking to the LRT, MRT, monorail and KTM Komuter. Take a Grab to your hotel to drop bags (most hotels hold luggage before check-in), freshen up and head out; Perdana Gardens is only a 5-minute ride back from KL Sentral if your hotel is in the centre.
tips: Buy the KLIA Ekspres ticket by tapping a contactless card at the gate - no queue.
Get a local eSIM or SIM (CelcomDigi, Maxis, U Mobile) at the arrivals hall for Grab; about RM30-50 for 7-30 days.
If your hotel is near KL Sentral, walk to Perdana Gardens via the National Mosque instead (20 min).
stops.hours: KLIA Ekspres about 05:00 to 00:30, every 15-20 min
stops.cost: KLIA Ekspres RM55 (~US$13); Grab to hotel RM10-20 (~US$2.50-5)
stops.from_previous: From KLIA T1/T2 by KLIA Ekspres, 28-33 min

stops.name: Perdana Botanical Gardens
stops.description: KL's oldest park, laid out in 1888 by British administrator Alfred Venning around a lake on the city's western edge, and still known as the Lake Gardens. Its 90 hectares of rolling lawns, rain trees and bamboo hold the Orchid and Hibiscus gardens, a lakeside walk with boats, a 'Laman Perdana' visitor area and a deer park. In the early morning it is full of joggers and tai-chi groups and is the quietest, greenest start to the trip. The newly reopened colonial mansion Seri Negara and the KL Bird Park sit on its edge.
tips: Enter by the Jalan Cenderawasih / Orchid Park side and loop the lake clockwise to the Sri Perdana colonnade and bamboo grove.
The Orchid & Hibiscus gardens charge a small fee on weekends only - Tuesday is free.
Skip the Bird Park (RM95+) unless you love birds; Seri Negara (Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00) is the better add-on if you have time.
Toilets and drinks at the Laman Perdana visitor centre by the lake.
stops.from_previous: From KL Sentral: Grab 5 min (RM6-8), or walk 20 min via the National Mosque

video.title: Perdana Botanical Garden Walking Tour: Kuala Lumpur

stops.name: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia
stops.description: Southeast Asia's largest museum of Islamic art, opened in 1998 in a white building crowned by five turquoise Iranian-tiled domes. Twelve permanent galleries cover Qur'an manuscripts, Ottoman and Mughal jewellery, Chinese-Islamic ceramics, arms and textiles, and superb scale models of the world's great mosques. The highlight is the Ottoman Room, a reconstructed 1820s Syrian reception room, and the painted inner domes seen from the upper floor. It is cool, uncrowded and beautifully lit - a perfect midday refuge.
tips: Start on level 1 with the architecture gallery (mosque models), then the Ottoman Room on level 2.
Look up from the upper-floor balconies at the inverted domes.
The museum restaurant serves good Middle Eastern lunch; the shop has quality books and textiles.
Masjid Negara (National Mosque) is next door if you want a quick outside look.
stops.cost: About RM20-25 (~US$5-6) for non-Malaysian adults (check iamm.org.my)
stops.from_previous: From Perdana Gardens: walk 10 min downhill past the Bird Park / Planetarium road

video.title: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia, Kuala Lumpur: A quick visit (2024)

stops.name: Old Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
stops.description: A 1910 Indo-Saracenic railway station of white domes, minarets and arches, facing the equally ornate KTM headquarters across the road. The front was restored in 2026 and the government has just announced a fuller restoration for tourism; it is still a working Komuter stop, so you can wander the old platforms. Opposite stands the KTM headquarters (1917), built in the same style by the same architect, A.B. Hubback, who also designed Masjid Jamek.
tips: The best photo is from the far side of Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, framing the domes against the sky.
Walk onto the old platforms via the Komuter entrance - nobody minds.
The Majestic Hotel next door does a well-known afternoon tea if you want a colonial break.
Parts of the facade may have scaffolding during the restoration announced in 2026.
stops.hours: Station open daily (working Komuter stop); facade 24 h
stops.from_previous: From Islamic Arts Museum: walk 8 min past Masjid Negara (use the pedestrian bridge over Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin)

video.title: Kuala Lumpur’s Hidden Gem: Old KL Railway Station (Most Underrated Spot?)

stops.name: Merdeka Square & Sultan Abdul Samad Building
stops.description: The former colonial cricket green where the Union Jack was lowered and Malaya's flag raised at midnight on 31 August 1957; a 95 m flagpole marks the spot. Facing it is the 1897 Sultan Abdul Samad Building, a copper-domed Moorish-Mughal fantasy with a 41 m clock tower, and on the other sides the mock-Tudor Royal Selangor Club, St Mary's Cathedral and the KL City Gallery. A few steps north, Masjid Jamek (1909) stands on the muddy confluence (kuala lumpur) of the Klang and Gombak rivers where the city was founded by tin miners in 1857.
tips: Walk to the River of Life viewpoint behind Masjid Jamek for the founding confluence and the mosque from the river side.
KL City Gallery has the I love KL sign and a giant city model - and air-conditioning.
The Textile Museum (free, 09:00-18:00) is the striking striped building at the south end.
Shade is scarce on the lawn; walk the arcades of Jalan Raja.
stops.hours: Open 24 h; KL City Gallery about 09:00-18:30
stops.from_previous: From Old Railway Station: walk 12 min north along Jalan Raja / Jalan Tun Perak, or Grab 5 min; lunch first at Central Market or Lot 10-style kopitiams in the arcades

video.title: Malaysia MERDEKA Square Kuala Lumpur 🇲🇾 Historical City Center! [ 4K ] Walking Tour

stops.name: Central Market (Pasar Seni) & Kasturi Walk
stops.description: A 1937 Art Deco wet market painted in powder blue, saved from demolition in the 1980s and turned into a crafts and culture market. Inside, two floors of stalls sell batik, songket weaving, wood carving, pewter and Malaysian snacks, arranged in themed 'lorong' (lanes) by ethnic group. Outside, the covered Kasturi Walk has wau (kite)-shaped roofing and food stalls. It is touristy but a useful, air-conditioned place to see Malaysian crafts in one go.
tips: Hand-drawn batik shops upstairs sell better pieces than the street stalls; expect to pay RM50-200 for a good sarong.
The food court on the upper floor is a cheap, cool lunch option (laksa, nasi campur).
Haggle gently on Kasturi Walk, not inside fixed-price shops.
stops.from_previous: From Merdeka Square: walk 8 min south across the river (Jalan Hang Kasturi)

video.title: 🇲🇾 KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA 4K Walking Tour | Central Market & Chinatown | Petaling Street 60 FPS

stops.name: Petaling Street, Chinatown & Kwai Chai Hong
stops.description: KL's Chinatown grew from Yap Ah Loy's 1860s Hakka mining settlement. Petaling Street is the covered market street (under a new roof since 2025), but the best of the area is around it: the 1873 Sri Mahamariamman Temple with its five-tier gopuram, the red Guan Di Temple opposite, the ornate Chan She Shu Yuen clan hall, and Kwai Chai Hong, a restored back lane of 1930s shophouses with murals of old Chinatown life and red lanterns. Coffee shops in restored shophouses and the REXKL arts space (a former cinema) make good rest stops.
tips: Loop: Kwai Chai Hong (enter from Jalan Petaling / Lorong Panggung) - Guan Di & Sri Mahamariamman temples on Jalan Tun H.S. Lee - Petaling Street market - Chan She Shu Yuen at the south end.
Try air mata kucing (monk-fruit drink) at the Petaling Street stall and chee cheong fun or a kopi at Kim Lian Kee / Old China Cafe.
Sri Mahamariamman: shoes off at the shoe counter (small fee); don't photograph priests during puja.
Upgrading works on Jalan Hang Lekir stalls run to end-Jan 2027; the rest of the market is open.
stops.hours: Market about 10:00-23:00; temples about 07:00-20:00; Kwai Chai Hong lane always open (shops vary)
stops.from_previous: From Central Market: walk 3 min east across Jalan Tun H.S. Lee

video.title: [4K] Petaling Street Market in Chinatown Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia 🇲🇾 Walking Tour Vlog & Travel Guide

stops.name: The View at 118 (Merdeka 118 observation deck)
stops.description: Merdeka 118 (completed 2023, 679 m to the tip of its spire) is the world's second-tallest building, shaped like faceted songket cloth and built next to Stadium Merdeka where independence was declared. Its observation deck, The View at 118, is scheduled to open on 15 December 2026 on levels 115-116, about 500 m up - the highest in Southeast Asia. Express lifts climbing 8-10 m per second take you up from the new 118 Mall; from the top you look down on the Petronas Towers, KL Tower and the whole Klang Valley, with the old Stadium Merdeka and Chinatown directly below. Optional extras (glass-floor edge experiences and a spire climb) are sold separately.
tips: Book a timed slot for about 17:45-18:15 online (theviewat118-online.globaltix.com) so you see daylight, sunset (~19:12) and the city lights coming on.
Entrance is inside 118 Mall, Lower Ground floor; allow 15-20 min for security and lift queues in the opening weeks.
West-facing windows get the sunset; the Petronas Towers are to the north-east - circle the deck twice.
If the sky is fully clouded in, ask about changing your slot or switch to the TRX park and do the deck another day.
stops.cost: Reports conflict: about RM150 (~US$35) for a foreign adult on one site, from RM30 on another. Confirm on the official site when booking.
stops.from_previous: From Chinatown: walk 12-15 min south-east via Jalan Hang Jebat / Stadium Merdeka, or MRT Pasar Seni - Merdeka (1 stop)

video.title: I Went Into Merdeka 118 In Kuala Lumpur - This Is What I Found!

stops.warning: Scheduled to open 15 Dec 2026, so it is brand new when you visit. Book a timed sunset slot as soon as sales open; holiday-week sunset slots will sell out. Check the opening actually happened before relying on it.

stops.name: TRX City Park (rooftop park at The Exchange TRX)
stops.description: A 10-acre landscaped park on the roof of The Exchange TRX mall, opened in late 2023, with lawns, water features and walking paths. From here the new skyline towers over you: Exchange 106 right above and Merdeka 118 in the distance. At night the lawns are softly lit and almost empty on a weekday, with Exchange 106 glowing directly above and Merdeka 118 to the west.
tips: Take the escalators to level 3 (the park level) from inside the mall; the north lawn has the best Merdeka 118 view.
Several of the park eateries stay open until ~22:00 for dinner; the mall food hall is another option.
In December the mall has big Christmas decorations; it's also a calmer NYE alternative (see KL3).
Skip it if you are tired - KLCC at night is the alternative (fountain shows ~20:00-22:00).
stops.hours: Park open daily from early morning until about 22:00-23:00; mall 10:00-22:00
stops.from_previous: From Merdeka 118: MRT Merdeka - TRX (Kajang line, 2 stops, ~10 min, RM2)

video.title: TRX City Park, Kuala Lumpur | 10-acre Rooftop Park Walking Tour | Malaysia Travel Guide

days.title: Batu Caves, Kampung Baru, the towers and a skyline sunset
days.summary: An early start beats the heat and crowds at Batu Caves, then a slow brunch in Kampung Baru, the old Malay village of wooden stilt houses, before crossing the Saloma Link bridge into the glass-and-steel world of KLCC. The afternoon climbs into the rainforest of Bukit Nanas and up KL Tower, and the day ends watching the skyline turn gold and then light up from the quiet hillside lookout on Changkat Tunku.
notes: Changed: KL Forest Eco Park and KL Tower moved here from KL3. On KL3 you get back from Putrajaya around 16:00 and the Eco Park closes at 16:30; KL Tower also tends to run ticketed countdown events on New Year's Eve. Both sit 1.5 km from KLCC, so they fit neatly after the towers today.

Identified: 'Changkat Tunku' is the Changkat Tunku Lookout Point, a free roadside viewpoint on the residential Bukit Tunku hill (Taman Duta), 4 km west of KLCC. It faces east, so the sun sets behind you and lights up the towers - it is a golden-hour and blue-hour skyline view, not a sun-on-the-horizon sunset.

Storm plan: if a thunderstorm hits mid-afternoon (common in December), the Eco Park canopy walk and KL Tower Sky Deck close; swap to Suria KLCC, Petronas Gallery or ILHAM Gallery and keep KL Tower's enclosed Observation Deck for the evening (open to ~22:00).

Cut first if tired: KL Forest Eco Park (or do it with KL Tower as one 1.5 h stop), then Titiwangsa. Wednesday: everything on this day is open (Eco Park closes Fridays; Petronas Skybridge closes Mondays).

15-night version (arriving Wed 30 Dec): merge KL1 + KL2 into one day - land, drop bags, Merdeka Square - Central Market - Chinatown (11:00-14:30), Grab to Kampung Baru + Saloma Link + KLCC Park (15:00-17:30), then Merdeka 118 at sunset (18:00-19:45). Cut Perdana Gardens, Islamic Arts Museum, Old Railway Station, TRX park, Eco Park, KL Tower, Changkat Tunku and Titiwangsa. Move Batu Caves to 07:30 on 31 Dec in place of Thean Hou + Brickfields, then continue to Putrajaya as planned (Grab Batu Caves - KL Sentral 25 min).

stops.name: Sunrise from the hotel
stops.description: Sunrise is about 07:12, roughly behind the Petronas Towers when seen from the west and south-west of the city, so a tower-facing room or rooftop catches the first light on the glass. Even on a hazy morning the towers turn pink-gold for ten minutes. Grab a coffee and watch from the room or the pool deck before heading north to Batu Caves.
tips: Ask the hotel the night before whether the rooftop/pool deck opens before 07:00 (many open at 07:00).
If your room faces away, Changkat Tunku (tonight's sunset spot) is also a classic sunrise viewpoint - but Batu Caves is the better use of this morning.
stops.from_previous: At your hotel

stops.name: Batu Caves
stops.description: A 400-million-year-old limestone hill whose huge cavern has been a Hindu shrine to Lord Murugan since 1891. A 42.7 m golden statue of Murugan (2006) guards the 272 rainbow-painted steps up to the Temple Cave, a 100 m-high chamber open to the sky where priests perform puja and macaques roam. At the foot are the Ramayana Cave with painted dioramas and a giant Hanuman, and the Cave Villa. Early morning brings soft light on the stairs, the sound of temple bells and far fewer tour groups.
tips: Arrive before 08:30: by 10:00 tour buses and heat take over.
Knees and shoulders must be covered; sarongs are lent or rented (a few RM) at the foot of the stairs.
Hold sunglasses, food and plastic bags tightly - the macaques snatch them on the stairs.
The Ramayana Cave (RM5) is worth 15 minutes; the separate Dark Cave conservation tours have been suspended in recent years, so don't plan on them.
stops.cost: Free (Temple Cave); Ramayana Cave RM5 (~US$1.20); Cave Villa ~RM15
stops.from_previous: From the city centre: Grab 25-30 min (RM20-35, ~US$5-8) - easiest early; or KTM Komuter KL Sentral - Batu Caves, ~35 min, about RM3, trains roughly every 30 min

video.title: Inside Batu Caves | Hidden Temple World of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia | 4K HDR Walking Tour

stops.name: Kampung Baru & Saloma Link bridge
stops.description: Kampung Baru was set aside in 1900 as a Malay agricultural settlement, and has resisted a century of redevelopment pressure: wooden stilt houses with carved eaves, banana trees and mosque domes still sit a few hundred metres from the Petronas Towers. Walk the lanes around Masjid Jamek Kampung Baru (1924) and Jalan Raja Muda Musa, the food street, for a late nasi lemak breakfast. Then cross the Saloma Link (2020), a 370 m curving pedestrian bridge over the Klang River and highway named after the 1950s singer Saloma, with the towers straight ahead - the classic 'old KL meets new KL' view.
tips: Brunch: Nasi Lemak Wanjo or the stalls along Jalan Raja Muda Musa; try kuih (sweet cakes) and teh tarik.
Best old houses: the lanes between Jalan Raja Abdullah and Jalan Raja Muda Musa; be discreet with cameras, these are family homes.
The Saloma Link has a viewing deck mid-span; it is also lit with changing LED colours after dark if you come back at night.
stops.hours: Village and bridge open 24 h; food stalls roughly 07:00-11:00 and evenings
stops.from_previous: From Batu Caves: Grab 25-30 min (RM20-30) to Masjid Jamek Kampung Baru; or Komuter back to Bank Negara + 15 min walk

video.title: How to Walk to KAMPUNG BARU from PETRONAS TWIN TOWERS (KLCC) via the Saloma Bridge | Kuala Lumpur
video.channel: Ummi Goes Where? | Malaysian Solo Traveler

stops.name: Petronas Twin Towers & KLCC Park
stops.description: The 452 m Petronas Towers (1998, architect Cesar Pelli) were the world's tallest buildings until 2004 and are still the tallest twin towers; their eight-pointed floor plan is based on the Islamic Rub el Hizb star, and the steel-and-glass facades shine silver in the midday sun. Behind them, the 20-hectare KLCC Park by Brazilian landscape architect Roberto Burle Marx has a lake with the Lake Symphony fountain, rainforest trees and a jogging track. Lunch and air-conditioning are in Suria KLCC mall at the towers' base.
tips: Classic photo: from the park side of the lake, or the Jalan P. Ramlee/Jalan Ampang corner with a wide lens.
The Skybridge (level 41-42 + level 86) is optional: about RM100 for foreigners, timed tickets, Tue-Sun; book ahead at petronastwintowers.com.my if you want it.
Galeri Petronas (art, level 3 Suria) and ILHAM Gallery (free, 10 min walk) are good storm shelters.
Come back at night for the fountain shows (about 20:00, 21:00, 22:00) if you skip Changkat Tunku.
stops.hours: Park daily ~07:00-22:00; Suria KLCC 10:00-22:00; Skybridge Tue-Sun ~09:00-21:00
stops.from_previous: From Kampung Baru: walk across the Saloma Link then 10 min along Jalan Ampang (total ~15-20 min)
stops.image_credit: Takeshi Aida from Hong Kong, Hong Kong, CC BY-SA 2.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:KLCC_Park_Petronas_Twin_Towers_%2853331134437%29.jpg

video.title: [4K] Petronas Twin Towers KLCC Park Water Fountain Show Kuala Lumpur Malaysia 🇲🇾 Night Walking Tour

stops.name: KL Forest Eco Park canopy walk (Bukit Nanas)
stops.description: Malaysia's oldest protected forest (gazetted 1906), a patch of real rainforest in the middle of the city. A canopy walkway of suspended bridges runs through the treetops with glimpses of KL Tower and the skyscrapers, and short trails lead past giant trees and macaque troops. The canopy walk is about 200 m long and up to 21 m above the forest floor; three short trails (Jelutong, Arboretum, Penarahan) loop through giant dipterocarp trees, and a path leads up to the KL Tower compound so you can combine both.
tips: Enter from Jalan Ampang (near Bukit Nanas monorail) or Jalan Raja Chulan; pay cash at the gate.
Do the canopy walk first (it shuts in heavy rain) and exit uphill via the KL Tower side.
Wear shoes with grip; bring water - there's nothing for sale inside.
Keep bags closed; macaques and silvered leaf monkeys are common.
stops.hours: Daily 08:00-16:30, closed Fridays (Wed 30 Dec is fine); closes in storms
stops.cost: Non-Malaysian adult RM40 (~US$9.50), cash only; canopy walk included
stops.from_previous: From KLCC: walk 20 min west along Jalan Ampang, or Grab 5 min (RM6-8)

video.title: Discover Kuala Lumpur Forest Eco-Park (formerly  Bukit Nanas Forest Reserve) | Experience Sharing

stops.name: KL Tower (Menara Kuala Lumpur)
stops.description: Completed in 1995 on top of Bukit Nanas, the 421 m telecom tower is taller-feeling than the Petronas Towers because it starts on a hill. The enclosed Observation Deck (276 m) has a 360-degree view; above it the open-air Sky Deck (300 m) and the glass-floored Sky Box let you stand over the city edge. The view is the best one of the Petronas Towers and Merdeka 118 together, and on clear afternoons you can see the Genting highlands on the horizon (the traveler's 'photo of KL + Genting').
tips: Buy online at kltower.com.my; the Sky Deck/Sky Box combo is worth it if the weather is clear.
The Sky Deck closes in rain and lightning - check the sky before paying for it; the Observation Deck stays open.
Shuttle vans run from the Jalan Punchak gate to the top if you don't walk up from the Eco Park.
stops.cost: Foreigners: Observation Deck roughly RM65-105 (~US$15-25); Sky Deck/Sky Box combos roughly RM120-190 (~US$28-45) - check current prices
stops.from_previous: From KL Forest Eco Park: walk up the trail to the tower compound, 5-10 min

video.title: KL Tower Sky Deck Sky Box & Observation Deck | Things To Do in Kuala Lumpur Malaysia

stops.name: Sunset at Changkat Tunku Lookout Point
stops.description: A small, free roadside lookout on Changkat Tunku, a quiet road of embassies and hillside mansions on Bukit Tunku (Kenny Hill) just north of the Lake Gardens. From the edge you see the whole skyline in one frame: KL Tower, the Petronas Towers, Exchange 106 and Merdeka 118, about 4 km away. As the sun sets behind the hill at about 19:12 the towers glow orange, then the city lights come on during blue hour (19:20-19:40). It is a local favourite with photographers and has no stalls or crowds.
tips: Address for Grab: 21 Changkat Tunku, Taman Duta, 50480 Kuala Lumpur; ask the driver to wait or book the return Grab a few minutes before you leave (residential area, few cars at night).
Bring a tripod or rest the camera on the wall for blue-hour shots; a 70-200 mm-type zoom compresses the towers nicely.
Keep voices low and don't block driveways - it is a residential street.
If clouds hide the towers, go straight to Titiwangsa or KLCC Park for the night view instead.
stops.from_previous: From KL Tower: Grab 15-25 min in evening traffic (RM12-20)

video.title: Experience the Best View of Kuala Lumpur: Changkat Tunku Lookout Point!

stops.name: Puncak Alop hilltop lookout (alternative sunset)
stops.description: A hilltop viewpoint above the old Ampang Lookout that reopened in March 2026 after a full redevelopment. The main platform, Puncak Hauz, looks across the whole skyline: Petronas Towers, Merdeka 118, Exchange 106 and KL Tower, with a cafe and restaurant on site. It is much higher and further out than Changkat Tunku (on the Ampang - Hulu Langat hill road, east of the city), so the skyline appears as a wall of towers rising from the plain with the sunset sky beyond it.
tips: Choose this instead of Changkat Tunku if you want food, toilets and a terrace; choose Changkat Tunku if you want closer towers and no travel.
Book the return Grab before it gets dark; the hill road has few cars at night.
The full site (glamping, observation tower) is due by the end of 2027; only phase one is open.
stops.cost: Free entry; food and drinks at Puncak Hauz cafe; Grab RM30-45 each way (~US$7-11)
stops.from_previous: From KL Tower: Grab 30-40 min in evening traffic

video.title: Puncak ALOP (April 2026)

stops.warning: In Selangor: not a forest reserve, so not covered by the 16 Nov-31 Jan forest closure as far as reported, but check it is open on the day.

stops.name: Titiwangsa Lake Gardens
stops.description: A large lake park north of the centre, built in the 1980s around old tin-mining pools, where locals jog, paddle boats and picnic. From the western shore the lake reflects the whole skyline, with KL Tower and the Petronas Towers side by side - one of the best free night views in the city and very peaceful on a weekday.
tips: Walk the path on the west/north-west side of the lake for the reflection shot.
Easy by Grab from Changkat Tunku (10-15 min), or Titiwangsa station (LRT/MRT/monorail).
Also a good morning alternative to the hotel sunrise.
stops.hours: Park open daily (paths lit in the evening)
stops.from_previous: From Changkat Tunku: Grab 10-15 min (RM10-15)

video.title: Exploring Titiwangsa Lake Gardens 🇲🇾 | Kuala Lumpur’s Most Beautiful Park

days.title: Thean Hou, Brickfields, Putrajaya - then New Year's Eve
days.summary: A Chinese temple on a hill at opening time and an Indian breakfast in Brickfields, then a fast train south to Putrajaya, Malaysia's planned government city of grand mosques and boulevards around a man-made lake. Back in KL by mid-afternoon to rest and swim before the New Year's Eve fireworks over the Petronas Towers.
notes: Changed: KL Forest Eco Park and KL Tower moved to KL2 (Eco Park closes 16:30, you return from Putrajaya ~16:00; KL Tower is busy with countdown events tonight). The afternoon is now a deliberate rest/pool block (16:30-19:30) before a late night.

Putrajaya mosque windows for non-Muslims (Sat-Thu): 09:00-12:30, 14:00-16:00, 17:30-18:00. Thursday 31 Dec is a normal visiting day; the plan puts Putra Mosque in the morning window and the Iron Mosque in the 14:00 window.
31 Dec is a normal working day in Malaysia (1 Jan is the public holiday); expect heavier traffic into the city centre from 17:00 and road closures around KLCC and Bukit Bintang from the evening.
Cut first if tired: Brickfields (have breakfast at the hotel), then the Palace of Justice photo stop. Keep the rest/pool block - you fly next morning.

stops.name: Thean Hou Temple
stops.description: A six-tiered Chinese temple completed in 1989 by the Hainanese community on Robson Heights, dedicated to Thean Hou (Mazu), the Heavenly Mother and protector of seafarers, alongside Guan Yin and the goddess of the waterfront. Its red pillars, curved tiled roofs and hundreds of red lanterns make it one of the most photogenic temples in Malaysia, and the terrace looks out over the city skyline. Early morning is calm: worshippers light incense, and the courtyard with the 12 Chinese zodiac statues is empty.
tips: Climb to the top prayer hall level first, then the side terraces for the lanterns with the skyline behind.
Shake the fortune sticks (kau cim) at the side altar and get your printed fortune - a small donation is customary.
Opening is reported as 08:00 (some sites say 09:00); if the hall is closed, the terraces and grounds are still worth it.
stops.from_previous: From KLCC/Bukit Bintang hotels: Grab 15-20 min (RM12-18); no convenient train

video.title: 🇲🇾 KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia - Thean Hou Temple walking Tour【4K HDR 60FPS】

stops.name: Brickfields (Little India): breakfast and temple walk
stops.description: KL's most vibrant Indian quarter: banana-leaf rice restaurants, flower-garland stalls and Tamil music along Jalan Tun Sambanthan. Within a few blocks are the Sri Kandaswamy Kovil (a Sri Lankan Tamil temple), the Buddhist Maha Vihara (founded 1894) and old churches, showing KL's many faiths side by side. In the morning the street is quieter than in the evening: flower-garland sellers set up, temple bells ring at the first pujas and the banana-leaf restaurants serve thosai and teh tarik.
tips: Breakfast: thosai, idli or appam with teh tarik at a Jalan Tun Sambanthan restaurant (Vishal, Sri Paandi and others), RM8-15.
Sri Kandaswamy Kovil (1909) has morning puja; shoes off, cover knees.
The Buddhist Maha Vihara (1894) on Jalan Berhala is calm and welcomes visitors.
KL Sentral is a 5-10 min walk for the Putrajaya train.
stops.hours: Shops and restaurants from ~07:00; temples roughly 06:00-12:00 and 16:00-21:00
stops.from_previous: From Thean Hou Temple: Grab 5-8 min (RM7-10)

video.title: Kuala Lumpur's Little India: A Sensory Overload (in the BEST Way!)

stops.name: Putrajaya: Putra Mosque, Dataran Putra, Perdana Putra, Persiaran Perdana, Palace of Justice, Iron Mosque
stops.description: Putrajaya has been Malaysia's federal administrative capital since 1999, a garden city built from scratch on former oil-palm land around a 650-hectare artificial lake. The pink-granite Putra Mosque (1999) seats 15,000 and mixes Persian, Malay and Arab design; next to it is Dataran Putra, the circular main square, and the green-domed Perdana Putra, the Prime Minister's office (outside view only). The 4 km Persiaran Perdana boulevard runs south past ministries to the Moorish Palace of Justice and across the lake to the Tuanku Mizan Zainal Abidin Mosque (2009), nicknamed the Iron Mosque because 70% of it is steel, with a white mesh facade and a glass-walled prayer hall that feels light and modern. Suggested order: KLIA Transit 10:15 - Grab to Putra Mosque (visit 11:00-12:00) - lunch at the lakeside food court under the mosque (Selera Putra) - Dataran Putra and Perdana Putra photos - Grab along Persiaran Perdana to the Palace of Justice (13:30) - Iron Mosque in the 14:00-16:00 window - Grab back to Putrajaya Sentral (~15:15).
tips: Train: KLIA Transit from KL Sentral (not the Ekspres) to 'Putrajaya & Cyberjaya', ~20 min, every 20-30 min. Alternative: MRT Putrajaya Line from central KL to Putrajaya Sentral (~60 min, cheaper).
Use Grab between sights (RM6-12 per hop): the city is spread out, shadeless and hot; Nadi Putra buses are infrequent and the new autonomous P113 bus runs weekdays only on a short loop.
Mosques lend robes and headscarves free at the entrance; men in shorts also need a robe. Go in through the visitors' entrance (signed) and stay out of the prayer hall during prayers.

Best photos: Putra Mosque from the lake promenade below Dataran Putra; the Iron Mosque from inside the prayer hall looking through the glass walls; Seri Wawasan bridge from the lakeside if you have time.
stops.cost: Mosques free; KLIA Transit ~RM14 (~US$3.30) each way (fares rise 1 Jan 2027); Grab hops RM6-12; lunch RM10-20
stops.from_previous: From Brickfields: walk 5-10 min to KL Sentral, KLIA Transit 20 min to Putrajaya & Cyberjaya, then Grab 10 min (RM8-12)

video.title: Putra Mosque (Pink Mosque) Putrajaya 4K 🇲🇾 Walking Tour Inside & Around | Malaysia

stops.name: New Year's Eve: fireworks over KL
stops.description:
KL's biggest midnight fireworks are launched around the Petronas Towers and KLCC Park, where last year's 'Rhythm of KLCC' concert started at 18:30 with a tower light show before midnight. Other displays usually go off at The Exchange TRX (light show from 20:00, fireworks at midnight seen from TRX City Park), around Pavilion/Bukit Bintang (the national Visit Malaysia countdown in 2025/26) and at KL Tower (fireworks since 2024/25 plus a ticketed party). Merdeka 118 and Dataran Merdeka have not had public fireworks in recent years. The 2026/27 programmes are normally announced in mid-December - check The Star / Malay Mail 'countdown hotspots' lists around 20-28 Dec.
Best strategy: (1) Calmest and best: a KLCC-area hotel with a tower-facing room and rooftop pool - swim at sunset (pools close ~22:00-23:00), dinner, then the fireworks from the room, the hotel's rooftop bar or its New Year party. (2) Free, in the crowd: KLCC Park esplanade by the lake; crowds build from 18:00, aim to be in by 20:00-21:00, then walk 5-10 min to Persiaran KLCC or Ampang Park stations rather than KLCC station afterwards. (3) Relaxed outdoor: TRX City Park - arrive 19:00-20:00, more space, toilets and food, fireworks overhead and the Petronas display in the distance. (4) Splurge: ticketed rooftop countdowns (Traders SkyBar, W's WET Deck, Sky51 at The Troika, Park Hyatt's Cacao on level 75 of Merdeka 118, Heli Lounge) - book by early December.
tips: Trains: last year Rapid KL ran LRT/MRT/monorail until about 02:00-03:00 with extra trains from 19:30 - check the MyRapid PULSE app for 2026/27 times.
Roads around Jalan Ampang, P. Ramlee, Sultan Ismail, Bukit Bintang and Tun Razak close or jam from the evening; Grab is surge-priced and near-useless 22:00-02:00 - stay within walking distance.
Banned in KLCC Park: fireworks, large flags/banners, noisemakers; bags may be checked. Bring water and a fully charged phone; mobile data slows to a crawl near midnight.
You fly to Bangkok in the morning: pack before going out and aim to be in bed by 01:30.
stops.cost: Free outdoors; hotel/rooftop countdown packages from roughly RM200 to RM2,000+ (~US$50-480)
stops.from_previous: From the hotel: walk (KLCC/Bukit Bintang); avoid driving after 18:00

video.title: Kuala Lumpur 2026: New Year's Eve countdown at KLCC Twin Towers with amazing Fireworks

stops.warning: 2026/27 event line-up not yet announced (usually mid-December). Book a tower-view hotel room or rooftop countdown ticket now; NYE rooms near KLCC sell out and may have 2-night minimums.

extras.name: FRIM Forest Skywalk (Kepong)
extras.description: The Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM), founded in 1929, replanted 545 hectares of worn-out tin-mining and vegetable land in Kepong with native trees; a century later it is a mature lowland rainforest and part of Malaysia's UNESCO-listed Kepong Botanic Gardens bid area. Its Forest Skywalk (opened 2019, replacing the old 1992 canopy walkway) links 11 towers of 18-50 m with eight bridges over 250 m; from the 50 m top tower you look over an unbroken canopy to the KL skyline. The walk to the start is a 30-40 minute uphill forest trail, so it is a real (short) jungle outing.
tips: Book a timed slot at skywalk.frim.gov.my and check FRIM's Facebook page the day before - the skywalk closes in heavy rain and for maintenance.
Go for the first slot (08:30): cooler, birds and dusky leaf monkeys are active, and afternoon storms are common in December.
Wear proper shoes and bring water; it's 30-40 min uphill from the car park to the skywalk entrance.
Pairs best with Batu Caves - they are 20 min apart by Grab, both north of the city.
extras.hours: Skywalk Sat-Thu about 08:30-12:30 and 14:30-15:30 (last slots), closed Fridays; closes in rain
extras.cost: FRIM entry a few RM per person plus Skywalk ticket for foreigners roughly RM30-50 (~US$7-12) - check current price on the booking site
extras.from_previous: From KL city: Grab 30-40 min (RM25-40); from Batu Caves Grab 20 min
extras.warning: Selangor's forest closure (16 Nov 2026-31 Jan 2027) covers state Forest Eco Parks and hiking in permanent forest reserves; FRIM is a federal institute and 2026 coverage shows the skywalk operating, but closure in bad weather is common - confirm the week before.
extras.what_to_swap: KL2 morning: Batu Caves 07:30-09:00, then FRIM 09:30-12:00; drop Kampung Baru brunch (cross Saloma Link at night instead) and go straight to KLCC after lunch. Or on KL3 instead of Thean Hou + Brickfields, starting Putrajaya after lunch (Iron Mosque 14:00, Putra Mosque 15:00).

extras.name: Pulau Ketam (Crab Island) fishing village
extras.description: A Chinese fishing village built on stilts over mangrove mudflats, reached by a 30-45 minute ferry from Port Klang. Walk the plank lanes past colourful houses and temples, rent a bicycle and eat a seafood lunch of crab and chilli prawns. Founded by Hokkien and Teochew fishermen in the 1870s, the village still runs on fishing and seafood, with almost no cars - just bicycles and walkways over the mud.
tips: KTM Komuter (Port Klang line) from KL Sentral to Pelabuhan Klang, then walk to the South Port passenger jetty for the ferry.
Rent a bike on the island (RM5-10) to reach the quieter Hokkien village and mangroves.
Go early; last ferries back are about 17:30 on weekdays, which still leaves time for New Year's Eve.
extras.cost: Train ~RM5 (~US$1); ferry ~RM10 each way (~US$2.50); seafood lunch RM40-80 (~US$10-20)
extras.from_previous: From KL Sentral: KTM Komuter to Pelabuhan Klang (~1 h 20) + ferry 30-45 min
extras.what_to_swap: Replaces Putrajaya on KL3 (keep Thean Hou early, skip Brickfields). Only if you would rather have a slow fishing-village day than grand architecture.

transport_out: Fri 1 Jan 2027 (public holiday in Malaysia), Kuala Lumpur (KUL) to Bangkok: about 2 h 05 flying, and Thailand is 1 hour behind Malaysia, so a 10:00 departure lands about 11:05 Bangkok time. Options: AirAsia (AK/FD) from KLIA Terminal 2 to Don Mueang (DMK), around 10 flights a day from ~06:00, typically RM150-400 (~US$35-95) with a bag; Malaysia Airlines (MH) and Thai Airways (TG) from KLIA Terminal 1 to Suvarnabhumi (BKK), roughly US$100-220; Batik Air (OD) from T1 to DMK. Check which terminal is on your ticket: T1 and T2 are 3 min apart by KLIA Ekspres but 15+ min apart otherwise. For BKK1 (Grand Palace last entry ~15:30) pick a departure between about 08:30 and 11:00: e.g. a 10:00 flight means leaving a KLCC hotel at 07:00, Grab to KL Sentral (10-15 min, quiet roads on the holiday morning), KLIA Ekspres (first train ~05:00, every 15-20 min; RM65 from 1 Jan 2027) to arrive by 08:00, two hours before departure. A direct Grab from KLCC to KLIA is 50-65 min and about RM75-110; on the morning after New Year's Eve, book it the night before or allow extra time for surge pricing. Bangkok airport choice: DMK (AirAsia) has the SRT Red Line to Krung Thep Aphiwat then MRT, or a 35-50 min taxi to the old town; BKK (full-service) has the Airport Rail Link to Phaya Thai then a taxi, 45-60 min to Rattanakosin - on New Year's Day traffic is light, so taxi/Grab from either airport is easiest (~300-450 THB). Book now: holiday fares rise sharply in December. Before landing, complete the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online within 3 days of arrival.
